purpose: §7-9: search for anything capable of deleting Company/company-owned state, and specifically the Prisma empty-predicate hazard pattern.
searchesPerformed: grep -rn 'deleteMany|TRUNCATE|DROP|reset|migrate reset|db push --force-reset|Company.delete|company.delete|raw DELETE|raw TRUNCATE' across tests/scripts/lib/prisma/package.json (scoped away from node_modules and stale .claude/worktrees copies to avoid false signal from historical/dead code)
grep -n 'company\.deleteMany\(\s*\)|deleteMany\(\{\s*\}\)|deleteMany\(\{\s*where:\s*\{\s*\}\s*\}\)' (the specific catastrophic empty-predicate pattern) across tests/, scripts/, lib/, prisma/
grep -n 'const where.*\?.*:.*\{\}' (the dynamic-filter-collapses-to-empty-object hazard pattern named in §9) across tests/scripts/lib

results.catastrophicEmptyPredicatePattern: ZERO MATCHES anywhere in tests/, scripts/, lib/, or prisma/. No `company.deleteMany()`, `deleteMany({})`, or `deleteMany({ where: {} })` exists in this codebase.
results.dynamicFilterCollapseHazard: ZERO MATCHES for the `const where = cond ? {...} : {}` anti-pattern.
results.generalDeleteManyUsage: 310 total `deleteMany(` occurrences across 76 test files, essentially all of the form `deleteMany({ where: { companyId: <exact-fixed-string> } })` or scoped to a specific test-owned id/prefix - the repository's own established, correct convention (per §16's own recommendation, already in wide use, not something this incident needs to introduce from scratch). A full line-by-line audit of all 310 was NOT performed (impractical given the evidence below made it unnecessary) - the static guard built in 12-destructive-guards.json/scripts covers this pattern class going forward automatically rather than relying on a one-time manual audit staying complete.
results.prismaCliCommands: package.json's own `"prisma:migrate": "prisma migrate dev"` script is present and would be the natural command a developer/agent types when adding a new migration. THIS is a live, present-tense footgun (see 09) - not itself proof of what happened, but a standing hazard independent of any application code.

conclusionForThisSection: No application-level or test-level destructive-call defect was found. This inventory, combined with 09's direct Postgres server-log evidence, shifts the finding away from the pre-incident working hypothesis ('a test's overly-broad deleteMany() wiped the Company table') toward Prisma's own CLI migration tooling running concurrently and unguarded against a shared database - see 09 for the full root-cause synthesis.
